thread.title: Bitcoin Reverses As Gold Keeps Rising; Apple Tests Support Again

author: NANCY GONDO
title: Bitcoin Reverses As Gold Keeps Rising; Apple Tests Support Again
text:
Stocks extended losses on the final trading day of 2017 as Apple ( AAPL ) weighed on the Dow Jones industrial average but Bitcoin reversed higher.
X PowerShares QQQ Trust ( QQQ ) fell 0.4%, while SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ( DIA ) and SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ) each gave up less than 0.2%. Emerging markets outperformed again as iShares MSCI Emerging Markets ( EEM ) rose 0.7%.
Banks, telecom and semiconductors led the downside among sector funds in the stock market today . Consumer staples, real estate and gold plays advanced. SPDR Gold Shares ( GLD ) and iShares Gold Trust ( IAU ) gained 0.7% each as gold futures jumped 1% to $1,309.50 an ounce and both ETFs extended their win streak to 10.
Oil stocks also gained: United States Oil ( USO ) advanced 0.8%, while PowerShares DB Oil ( DBO ) added 0.6%. West Texas intermediate crude prices were up 0.8% to $60.33 a barrel.
Apple, down 0.7%, was one of the Dow's biggest losers. Shares slid back to the 50-day moving average after climbing the prior two sessions. The iPhone maker is 4% below a 176.34 flat-base buy point cleared last week. It stumbled this week amid reports of weaker-than-expected demand for the iPhone X.
Bitcoin staged an upward reversal for a 0.7% gain to $14,527.74, but still below an early rise to $15,076.06, according to CoinDesk . The crypto currency has been extremely volatile since CME Group ( CME ) launched futures Dec. 18. Bitcoin Investment Trust ( GBTC ) recovered 6% but is still more than 40% off its Dec. 10 intraday peak.
Is Gold The New Bitcoin? While Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies have been getting all the attention, gold's recent advance has stayed under the radar.
The precious metal has gained more than 4% over the past two weeks and is now near $1,294.90, according to Kitco . Meantime, Bitcoin as tracked by Bitcoin Investment Trust ( GBTC ) has plunged 44% from Dec. 18 to Dec. 28.
Of course, GBTC is still up nearly 1,500% for the year compared with gold's 12% advance based on SPDR Gold Shares ( GLD ) and iShares Gold Trust ( IAU ). But is gold's increase due to the usual Chinese New Year-related sales, or could it be a longer-lasting shift?
GLD and IAU, which advanced for a ninth consecutive session Thursday, gapped up above their respective 50-day moving average lines on Tuesday. While both ETFs had undercut the 50-day too deeply to stage a rebound off the line, shares are testing earlier areas of upside resistance. These could offer early entry points if SPDR and IAU keep rising.
In a late August breakout past a 123.41 flat-base buy point, GLD rose 4% to its Sept. 7 intraday high. IAU advanced more than 3%, also from a late August breakout to a Sept. 7 peak.
Both funds track the price of gold bullion. GLD has amassed $34.4 billion since its November 2004 launch; IAU has attracted $10 billion since its January 2005 debut. Both ETFs have offered a 4.1% average annual return over the past 10 years vs. the S&P 500's 8.5% gain. GLD and IAU carry respective expense ratios of 0.40% and 0.25%.
Despite the drastic outperformance of Bitcoin or the equity market vs. gold, investors may want to consider rebalancing gold holdings in their portfolio, U.S. Global Investors CEO Frank Holmes said in a recent blog post . He suggests a 10% weighting in gold.
